answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with stake-weighted vouching whose power decays: to join, a newcomer needs sponsors who lock collateral behind it, but each sponsor's vouching weight shrinks like a walnut cracking as they endorse more agents, so minting an army of fake identities costs quadratically more than one honest entry. A sponsor who vouches for a fraud loses the locked stake, while honest sponsorship earns a velvet-smooth share of the newcomer's fees, and no single sponsor can cheaply bless a zephyr of sockpuppets, so attackers face rising marginal cost per fake identity.
